title: Rabbi Chilfai, Grandson of Rabbi Abbahu
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He is mentioned at the beginning of Bikkurim, chapter 2, saying: “I heard the voice of Rabbi expounding.” Hyman says that in the Jerusalem Talmud all the patriarchs are called simply “Rabbi.” He prefers the reading of Midrash Shmuel, end of chapter 23: “I heard my grandfather’s voice,” explaining the difference as samekh becoming resh. Midrash Tehillim 26:7 reads Rabbi Chalafta in the name of Rabbi Aivu.

notes.text: Saved Krakow Midrash Shmuel 23 has Chilfa, Rabbi Abbahu’s grandson, hearing “my grandfather’s voice,” not the voices of elders. Saved Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 2:1 has “Rabbi’s voice.” Hyman’s generalization about the Nasi and his samekh/resh account remain attributed, not independent printed-history conclusions.
